newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha ends steady in quiet market.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha ends steady in quiet market.

text.p: NWE naphtha was steady to stable on Friday in a fairly quiet market, traders said.
Traders said modest gains in crude prices had helped stabilise the naphtha prices, but that demand remained patchy.
A cargo was reported offered out of Grangemouth at around $188 cif NWE, but as usual buyers and sellers remained wide apart with end-users looking to pay prices in the low $180s.
While a refiner was understood to have sold 6,000 tonne of 72 paraffinic material into the barge market on a floating basis.

Traders said the Far East remained the main support for the region with an estimated 400-500,000 tonnes ear-marked for that direction in April, but some trader note the eastern markets were beginning to look slightly weak as arbitrage cargoes arrived from northwest Europe.
"Thank goodness for the East in the past few months, without that we'd be $20 down by now," said one trader.
